title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks closed out the week with a Friday rally — S&P 500 and Nasdaq each +0.6%, Dow +0.8% (423 pts) — after a sharp Thursday tech selloff, capping a week of fresh record highs.

Markets: 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to 5.24% Friday (still down on the week) as Fed political drama simmers; Brent crude +0.4% to ~$104.72 on Gulf Coast output disruptions, and gold rallied toward $4,220.

Companies: SpaceX's move to buy wireless spectrum for its own mobile network hit telecom carriers hard (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon all -8%+) while cell-tower operators surged (Crown Castle +16%, American Tower +9%, SBA +7%).

Companies: Delta Air Lines cut its full-year profit outlook on a $6B jump in fuel costs, though shares closed roughly flat; Nvidia's AI-era accounting for free cash flow/buybacks is drawing fresh investor scrutiny.
Companies: Q3 earnings season kicks off next week — JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and other big banks report starting Tuesday, followed by BlackRock, Interactive Brokers and Marsh & McLennan.

Macro/Policy: Trump plans a White House hearing to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook, keeping political pressure on the central bank ahead of next week's September CPI (Wed), PPI (Thu) and the Fed's Beige Book (Wed).

Macro/Policy: AI's weight in the economy keeps growing — tech is now ~40% of S&P 500 market cap (above the dot-com peak), nearing 50% with Meta/Amazon included — a divide analysts flag as a growing market risk.
Macro/Policy: Axios reports AI industry leaders are privately war-gaming a 'day after' scenario for a major AI-driven cyberattack, bracing for political backlash against the sector.
